title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a manuscript note. It is an upside-down typescript page, 'IX - 56 -', from SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), §5.2. The archive stamped it 374 and foliated it 202. It was filed among the 1975-76 notes on the divided-power de Rham complex, but it has no mathematical connection to its neighbours. The previous page computes divided-power coordinate changes; the next page is about automorphisms of the simplicial PD algebras A_•(S,S^+,t).

Context. S is a base (the strict henselisation of a discrete valuation ring, with closed point o). A and A' are abelian varieties dual to each other, and A^o, A'^o are the identity components of their Néron models. T_ℓ(A^o) is the ℓ-adic Tate module, seen as a pro-ℓ Barsotti-Tate group over S. It has a filtration: toric part ⊂ fixed part (T^t ⊂ T^f), with abelian quotient T^ab. The biextension W of (A^o, A'^o) by G_m gives the pairing (5.2.4.2), T_ℓ(A^o)^f × T_ℓ(A'^o)^f → T_ℓ(G_m).

Goal. Prove the orthogonality theorem: the toric parts are mutually orthogonal, and the induced pairing on the abelian pieces is non-degenerate up to isogeny.

Lemma 5.2.5 (rigidity). Let u: G → H be a homomorphism of pro-ℓ Barsotti-Tate groups over S. If the fibre u_o at the closed point is zero, then u is zero. If u_o is an isogeny (resp. an isomorphism), so is u.

Application, in three steps.
1. Take the composite T_ℓ(A^o)^t → T_ℓ(A^o)^f → D(T_ℓ(A'^o)^f), where D is the Cartier/Tate dual. On the special fibre this composite is zero: the pairing kills the torus part by 5.2.4. So the composite is zero over S, and the pairing vanishes on the toric part on the left.
2. By symmetry it vanishes on the toric part on the right. It therefore descends to a pairing T^ab × T'^ab → T_ℓ(G_m). The quotients are again pro-ℓ Barsotti-Tate groups.
3. The map T^ab → D(T'^ab) is an isogeny because its special fibre is one. That fibre is the Weil pairing of the dual abelian parts B, B' of the special fibres.

The proof of 5.2.5 is left to the reader: it is easy and valid over any connected noetherian base. Grothendieck adds that 7.4.7 will give a direct proof of the two special cases used, via a finer analysis of the finite-level biextensions W_n of (A^o_n, A'^o_n).
errors: No mathematical error. 5.2.5 is a standard rigidity statement over a connected noetherian base. When ℓ is invertible, as in SGA 7 IX, the objects are lisse ℓ-adic sheaves and it is immediate. In general it rests on the height of the kernel/cokernel being locally constant, and on Hom of finite flat group schemes over a connected base being detected on fibres plus flatness. The 'facile' leaves those details implicit.
Archival oddity rather than an error: this published SGA 7 typescript page is misfiled among the PD de Rham notes.

ideas.what: Rigidity of homomorphisms of pro-ℓ Barsotti-Tate groups: zero, isogeny or isomorphism can be checked at one fibre over a connected noetherian base
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity for ℓ-divisible groups / lisse ℓ-adic sheaves

ideas.what: Orthogonality of toric parts under the biextension pairing, and non-degeneracy up to isogeny on the abelian pieces
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's orthogonality theorem for semistable reduction (monodromy pairing context)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX typescript, inserted into the archive file. Its content is fully published and credited to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: The image is upside down. Header 'IX - 56 - IX', archive stamps '374' and pencilled '202'.
The transcription is otherwise accurate. 'pro-ℓ-groupes' has a script ℓ, and 'démonstration' in the last paragraph is typed over a correction.
